articles.title: Google Chat’s latest feature could finally end the post-meeting confusion
articles.excerpt: Your meeting's biggest takeaways now land right where your team chats.
articles.body: TL;DR Google Chat is getting automatic AI-powered meeting recaps that summarize discussions, decisions, and assigned action items. Recaps appear directly in meeting chats, complete with links to Gemini notes, recordings, and transcripts, so participants can catch up without digging through files. The feature is rolling out gradually to eligible Google Workspace subscribers. There’s always that one meeting where everyone agrees on the next steps, only for half the team to forget who promised what by lunchtime. Then comes the frantic search through notes, recordings, and chat messages to piece everything together. Google wants to put an end to that familiar office headache with a new Google Chat feature that brings the important stuff straight into your conversations after a meeting.

articles.title: Fine-Tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA Explained: Which One Should You Use?
articles.excerpt: If you have started experimenting with large language models (LLMs), you have probably come across these terms: Fine-Tuning LoRA QLoRA Knowledge Distillation They are related, but they do not all desc…
articles.body: If you have started experimenting with large language models (LLMs), you have probably come across these terms: Fine-Tuning LoRA QLoRA Knowledge Distillation They are related, but they do not all describe the same thing. Understanding the differences can help you avoid wasting compute on the wrong training approach. Let's break them down. First: Why Customize an AI Model? Imagine you have a pretrained model that can generate text and answer general questions. You now want it to perform a specific task, such as: Generating structured customer-support responses. Following a specialized writing style. Extracting information into a predefined format. Handling domain-specific examples more reliably. You could train a model from scratch, but that is often unnecessary and expensive.

articles.title: LazyDesk 🦥 — Less Time Organizing Notes, More Time Getting Things Done
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady I built LazyDesk because turning a pile of notes into something useful shouldn't feel like another task on m…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built I built LazyDesk because turning a pile of notes into something useful shouldn't feel like another task on my to-do list. Think about a typical day: you write down an assignment deadline, a reminder to email someone, an idea you might explore later, and a few things you don't want to forget. Everything is there, but it's scattered. Before you can actually get to work, you have to sort it all out. That's the small problem LazyDesk tries to solve. LazyDesk is a local-first productivity app that takes messy notes and turns them into organized task checklists or concise summaries. You paste your notes, choose Organize tasks or Summarize notes, and let AI help with the first draft.

articles.title: Two Free Offers, Two Failure Modes: Route AI Work by Blast Radius, Not by Lane
articles.excerpt: Two tabs open. Both say free. One is a token allowance on a hosted model endpoint; the other is a server you can run somewhere. My platform lead looked at them and asked the reasonable question: "So w…
articles.body: Two tabs open. Both say free. One is a token allowance on a hosted model endpoint; the other is a server you can run somewhere. My platform lead looked at them and asked the reasonable question: "So which one do we take?" It took me a week to notice that the question was malformed. They are not two versions of the same offer. They fail in completely different ways, on different timelines, against different budgets. Choosing between them like flavors is how teams end up with a free model quota nobody trusts and a box nobody patches. Here is the reframe that actually helped: stop picking a lane for the team. Route individual change sets, and let the two offers absorb the classes of work they are genuinely good at.

I've experimented with quite a few website builders and nocode tools over the years, but SpreadSimple is one of those tools that really surprised me with how simple it is to use. articles.title: A Free Prerequisite Graph of Everything Kids Learn: Exploring Marble's os-taxonomy
articles.excerpt: If you have ever tried to build anything in education tech, you have probably hit the same wall: curriculum data is either a flat list of standards in a PDF, or it is locked inside someone's product.…
articles.body: If you have ever tried to build anything in education tech, you have probably hit the same wall: curriculum data is either a flat list of standards in a PDF, or it is locked inside someone's product. A flat list tells you what a child should learn in Year 2. It does not tell you what they need to know first . And that second question is the one that matters if you are building adaptive practice, a tutoring app, a learning-path generator, or an AI tutor that needs to know where a kid is stuck. os-taxonomy from Marble is an attempt to fix that. It is an open dataset that breaks primary and elementary learning into small, teachable ideas and connects them with prerequisite edges. It has picked up around 4.8k stars, which is a lot for a pure data repo.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 20 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you .

articles.body: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when you have hundreds of endings. Just look at how so much attention on Baldur's Gate 3 focused on its endings or, years before, how everyone tended to ignore the smaller ways the Mass Effect trilogy changed across three games in favor of looking at the restrictive outcomes in Mass Effect 3 .

articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
